full_judgment: 2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal are that one Md Mujtaba Siddique, son of late Mustafa Siddique was the original owner of the disputed property which was allotted to him by the Government of the then East Pakistan through a letter dated 23-1-1960. In pursuant to the aforesaid allotment letter, an agreement for lease of land measuring an area of 144 square yards or thereabout under the registration jurisdiction of Mohammadpur Sub-registry, Dhaka appertaining to Mouza-Baraba, Police Station-Tejgaon, now Mohammadpur, being Plot VI/15 in Block-D of the layout plan No.57 of 59/60 dated 6-8-1959 for a period of 99 years, was executed and registered on 26-1-1960 at the Sadar Sub-registrar Office, Dhaka being deed No.1542. Subsequently, the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique filed an application on 10-9-1963 praying for permission for constructing buildings thereon. The said original owner filed an application being No.1483 asking for a sanction of loan from the House Building Finance Corporation, Zonal Office, Dhaka and on 1 8-2-1964 the loan amounting to Taka 18,000 was granted in his favour. He also paid the Government dues in respect of his house amounting to Taka 18,000 and obtained a clearance certificate from the office of the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur, Mirpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka being Memo No.550-AO dated 25-2-1964. The aforesaid original lessee, Md Mujtaba Siddique obtained a certificate from the Section Officer, LG Department and Government of the then East Pakistan, who attested his specimen signatures as genuine, which was put on the original lease deed. The original lessee on 28-2-1994 executed and registered .a mortgage deed being No. EP-36292 (deed No.1673) in favour of the House Building Finance Corporation to avail the loan sanctioned for the construction of building. The original lessee also maintained a telephone and had been paying monthly bills regularly, he obtained a certificate in respect of payment of the telephone bills being No.T.R./312048. The original lessee paid the municipal taxes regularly to the Dhaka Municipal Committee and he also paid the electricity charges and bills to the Dhaka Electric Supply regularly. The due rent was paid to the Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka. On 14-12-1972, a deed of sale being deed No.23424 was executed by the original lessee in favour of Md Serajul Islam, the predecessor of the respondents, Police Station-Keraniganj, District-Dhaka in respect of transfer of the case property situated at 6/15 Razia Sultana Road, Block-D, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka at a consideration of Taka 35,000.
